newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN LENDING RATE DROPS TO 8.3 FROM 11 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN LENDING RATE DROPS TO 8.3 FROM 11 PCT.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate dropped to 8.3 on Thursday from 11 percent, with call money loans making up most of fresh trade, dealers said.
Total daily trade shrank to 34 million kuna ($5.1 million) against 115 million kuna on offer. New settlements accounted for 27 million kuna.
The interbank call money rate remained flat at 7.0 percent while one-month borrowings were made at 10 percent, down from 11 percent on Wednesday.
Banks rolled over previous loans at rates ranging between 8.0 percent for one-week funds and 12 percent for one-month money.
The kuna midrate firmed to 6.7024 against the dollar and to 3.563 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.643 Croatian Kuna)
